body:
## Problem

Sepo currently has fallback logic for weak `author_association` values on issue-body mentions, but the same normalization does not consistently apply to other mention-trigger surfaces such as discussion comments, issue comments, PR review comments, and review submissions.

GitHub webhook and GraphQL payloads can report a weak association such as `NONE` or `CONTRIBUTOR` even when the triggering user has repository access. When that weak value is passed directly into route authorization, otherwise valid requests can be rejected by `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY`.

## Mechanism

The existing issue path refreshes weak issue author associations from the live issue API and, when needed, checks repository collaborator status before policy evaluation. Non-issue mention surfaces still primarily trust the event payload association.

This creates inconsistent authorization behavior across surfaces:

- issue-body mentions can be upgraded after a live API/collaborator check
- discussion/comment/review mentions can remain stuck at a weak payload association
- dispatch policy then rejects the route even if the actor has repository access

## Proposed solution

Generalize the existing issue fallback into a shared weak-association normalization step for mention triggers.

Suggested approach:

1. Treat strong associations (`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`) as trusted without refresh.
2. For weak associations (`NONE`, `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIMER`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, etc.), identify the triggering actor login for the current event type.
3. Check repository collaborator/permission status with the GitHub API.
4. If the actor has repository access, normalize the association to `COLLABORATOR` before route policy evaluation.
5. Preserve the current issue-specific refresh where useful, but make the final collaborator fallback surface-agnostic.
6. Add regression tests for `discussion_comment`, `issue_comment`, and PR review/comment events where the payload association is weak but collaborator lookup succeeds.
7. Update access-policy docs to describe weak-association normalization across mention surfaces, not only issue-body mentions.

This should keep the trust boundary conservative: weak associations are only promoted when GitHub confirms repository access.

Checked. The issue is valid.

Current code already has the pieces, but they are scoped inconsistently:

- `extract-context` refreshes/promotes weak associations only inside `refreshIssueAssociation`, and that function returns early unless `eventName === "issues"`: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/extract-context.ts#L106-L158
- Other mention surfaces get the raw payload association via `getAuthorAssociation` for `issue_comment`, `discussion_comment`, PR review comments, and review submissions: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/context.ts#L83-L112
- That association is then passed directly into dispatch policy resolution: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L283-L295 and https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/resolve-dispatch.ts#L50-L60
- Tests currently cover issue-body promotion, but also preserve non-issue weak values like `issue_comment` `NONE` for later policy checks: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/extract-context-cli.test.ts#L180-L245 and https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/extract-context-cli.test.ts#L861-L905
- Docs also describe the fallback as issue-body-only: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/access-policy.md#L80-L82

So the proposed problem statement is accurate. The practical impact appears mainly when a repository tightens `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY` to exclude weak values such as `CONTRIBUTOR` or `NONE`; a real collaborator can then be rejected on comments/reviews/discussions even though issue-body mentions may be upgraded.

Recommended implementation scope:

1. Add a shared weak-association normalizer in `extract-context.ts`.
2. Treat `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, and `COLLABORATOR` as strong and return them unchanged.
3. Preserve the current issue-body REST refresh for `issues` events.
4. For weak associations on all mention surfaces, resolve the triggering actor with `getRequestedBy(eventName, payload)`.
5. Check repository permission/collaborator status and promote confirmed access to `COLLABORATOR`.
6. Add regressions for `issue_comment`, `discussion_comment`, `pull_request_review_comment`, and `pull_request_review`.
7. Update `access-policy.md` from “Issue-body association refresh” to mention-trigger weak-association normalization.

I recommend approving implementation with that scope.
